correctness.rationale: Exact proof: symmetry identifies multiplication with N independent basis-multiset vectors; spanning rank-one symmetric tensors is equivalent to the nonexistence of a degree-m homogeneous polynomial vanishing everywhere. A basis of evaluation columns gives a unique decomposition and an injective N-dimensional natural-basis ideal embedding, with total ambient product image in the ideal. Infinite fields satisfy polynomial identity; over F_q the induction on n plus degree m-1<q grid uniqueness proves spanning for m<=q, including characteristic dividing m!. For m>=q+1, the Frobenius identity mu(x^(m-1),y)=mu(x^(m-q),y^q) holds in any diagonal m-ary algebra but fails in the explicit symmetric multiplication on dimension two; zero padding handles all n>2. Three standalone exact computation scripts, rerun from their actual package source, confirm sampled rational, prime-field and extension-field cases; no finite test is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Question 4.7 of arXiv:2609.32784v1 explicitly asks whether finite-dimensional commutative m-ary algebras embed in m-ary evolution algebras; it does not assert the theorem. The 2026 paper proves the binary case (Theorem 2.1) and anticipates characteristic-zero or characteristic greater than m as sufficient, whereas the new proof establishes a sharp finite-cardinality criterion, includes arbitrary infinite-field characteristic, supplies constructive N-dimensional ideal envelopes, and proves an obstruction for all m>q. The classical homogeneous evaluation rank from projective Reed–Muller coding theory is credited and not claimed as new. Targeted published-finding corpus and external literature searches showed related binary envelope, projective-code, and general tensor work but no covering m-ary embedding theorem. Priority is conditional on the checked sources and access risks.
